title: Finite-stage finite-Tor-amplitude complexes form a triangulated subcategory
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a scheme $Y$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $D^b_c(Y,A)\subset D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated]. Let $P$ be the property of $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$: $K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ and $K$ has finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Then $P$ is closed under isomorphisms and defines a full triangulated subcategory of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: $0$ satisfies $P$; $K$ satisfies $P$ if and only if $K[m]$ does, for every $m\in\mathbf Z$ (if $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ then $K[m]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-m,b-m]$); and for every distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K$ and $M$ satisfying $P$, also $L$ satisfies $P$ (if $K$ and $M$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, so does $L$).

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.46.4 (Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude), part (2), for the ringed site $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(A_{E,n})_Y)$; together with lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated for the constructibility part

proof.text: Use Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing, the existing proof attached to def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, to obtain Finite A. Apply lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated to obtain the isomorphism and triangulated closure properties for bounded constructibility.

proof.text: For each degree-zero module sheaf M, use the proved general-universe K-flat resolution to choose a K-flat complex N quasi-isomorphic to M. The existing DerivedCategory.commShiftTensorRightQhObj and isTriangulated_tensorRightQhObj make tensor with Qh(N) an exact functor. For each K-flat presentation P of L, localized quasi-isomorphisms and the invertible lax tensor comparison give F(Q(L)) isomorphic to Q(P tensor M), exactly the derivedTensor object in def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude. This uses the same pro-etale site and lifted constant coefficient ring; no site comparison is made.

proof.text: For an isomorphism $K\cong L$, the functor $T_F$ sends it to an isomorphism, and the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] send that to isomorphisms $H^i(T_F(K))\cong H^i(T_F(L))$. Therefore vanishing outside any fixed interval is identical for $K$ and $L$. Also additivity gives $T_F(0)\cong0$: the identity of its value is the image of $1_0=0$ and hence is zero. All its cohomology objects are zero. By [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], zero has Tor amplitude in $[0,0]$, and finite Tor amplitude is invariant under isomorphisms. Step 1 supplies the constructibility clauses.

With the cohomological shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $(C[m])^i=C^{i+m}$ and its differential differs by the sign $(-1)^m$, which does not change kernels or images. Thus $H^i(C[m])\cong H^{i+m}(C)$. Combine this with Step 2 to get $H^i(T_F(K[m]))\cong H^{i+m}(T_F(K))$. If $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, these cohomology sheaves vanish for $i\notin[a-m,b-m]$, for every $F$. This is exactly the shifted Tor bound in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Conversely, apply the forward implication to $K[m]$ with shift $-m$ and use $(K[m])[-m]\cong K$. Step 1 supplies the bounded constructible equivalence.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude; Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor; cohomological shift convention

proof.text: Consider a distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$. If the endpoint Tor intervals are $[a_1,b_1]$ and $[a_2,b_2]$, set $a=\min(a_1,a_2)$ and $b=\max(b_1,b_2)$. Since each endpoint interval lies in $[a,b]$, both endpoints have Tor amplitude in this common interval by [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. For each degree-zero module sheaf $F$, Step 2 gives a distinguished triangle $T_F(K)\to T_F(L)\to T_F(M)\to T_F(K)[1]$. Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] in the abelian category of $A_Y$-modules. For $i\notin[a,b]$ the exact segment is $0=H^i(T_F(K))\to H^i(T_F(L))\to H^i(T_F(M))=0$, Exactness says that the image of the zero map into the middle object is the kernel of its zero map to zero. The former is zero and the latter is the whole middle object, so the middle object is zero. This works for every $F$, so $L$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. If the endpoint interval was already $[a,b]$, it stays unchanged. Step 1 shows that $L$ is bounded constructible as well.

proof.text: The full subcategory defined by the conjunction $P$ inherits the ambient morphisms. Steps 1 and 3 give zero and closure under isomorphisms; Step 4 gives all integer shifts and the reverse implication; Step 5 gives closure under extensions. These are precisely the hypotheses in [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], so the inherited shift and distinguished triangles make it a full triangulated subcategory, as asserted.
